why: If Koko finishes in time at speed k, she also finishes at any faster speed. That monotone yes/no lets you binary search the smallest working k in [1, max(piles)], with sum(ceil(p / k)) as the check.
hints: If speed k is fast enough, is k + 1 also fast enough?
Yes, so feasibility is a step from false to true. Binary search for the first true. The check: hours = sum of ceil(pile / k).
Search lo = 1, hi = max(piles); each check is O(n), giving O(n log max). Use (p + k - 1) // k for the ceiling.
pitfalls: Speed max(piles) always works since h >= n, so it is a safe upper bound.
Use integer ceiling, not float division.
Leftover time in an hour is wasted: a pile of 7 at speed 4 takes 2 hours.
